steps.answer:
Recorded h1: When batch size goes up, tail_heaviness goes higher. On these runs it is inconclusive. batch size 8 against 1: tail_heaviness 2.8086 against 2.7079, a gap of 0.1007. The gap is inside the seed spread within one setting (1.6831).
To settle it: 6 runs, batch size at 1 and 4, 3 seeds each, everything else as here. It is refuted if the higher batch size setting gives the lower tail_heaviness on every seed.
steps.args: {"formula":"tail_heaviness","formula_moves":"up","knob":"batch","knob_change":"raise","why":"Increasing the batch size may lead to more variance in latency, which could result in a heavier tail as indicated by an increase in tail_heaviness."}

steps.answer: Recorded h2: When batch size goes up, throughput_p50 goes higher. On these runs it is passes its test on these runs alone. batch size 8 against 1: throughput_p50 497.2172 against 181.6497, a gap of 315.5675. Every comparison of runs agrees: exact rank test p = 0.05.
